rv.q: Russell Beale anchors things, his performance carefully calibrated.

Russell Beale once again pulls off his great trick of being totally theatrical yet totally real as he mixes the larky and the intimate, the plaintive and the playful, speckling the well-spoken Foote with West Country vowels.
Mr Foote's Other Leg is a rambunctious, raucous ride of a play, galloping through the history of the time with a twinkle in its eye.

cn.t: Critics find this Hampstead transfer a flawed but affectionate love letter to theatre, elevated by Simon Russell Beale's performance. Structural issues persist, but the Haymarket setting adds welcome atmosphere to Kelly's overstuffed Georgian tragicomedy.
